title.en: Writing a report and a review

hook.en: A report says what happened, clearly and in order. A review says what something was like and whether it is worth your time. One is objective, the other evaluative.

objectives.en: Write a newspaper or school report in the correct format
Write a book or film review with a balanced judgement
Use the past tense and the passive voice where suitable

narration.en: A report says what happened, clearly and in order. A review says what something was like and whether it is worth your time. One is objective, the other evaluative.

body.en: A report gives a factual account of an event (a school function, an accident, an exhibition). Format: a heading, a byline, and the place and date. The opening answers the five Ws and H (what, when, where, who, why, how) in brief; the body gives details in order, with names, numbers and quoted reactions; the end gives the result or what next. A report is objective: no personal opinion beyond reported comments. It is written mainly in the past tense, often using the passive voice (The prizes were given away by …).

body.en: A review (of a book, film, play, exhibition or app) helps a reader decide. It names the work and its creator, gives a brief idea of the subject or plot without spoiling the ending, then evaluates: characters or performances, themes, style, strengths and weaknesses, with examples. It ends with a recommendation and who would enjoy it. A review is evaluative and personal, but fair: praise and criticism are both backed by reasons.
